obligations.requirement: All Category A and Category B1 projects must undertake Public Consultation, comprising a district-wise public hearing at or near the site conducted by the State Pollution Control Board, plus written responses from other concerned persons. Where the site spans more than one district, a hearing is required in each.
obligations.trigger: Category A or B1. Category B2 is exempt, as are building and township projects, projects inside approved industrial estates, highway expansion without further land acquisition, irrigation modernisation, and defence or strategic projects.
obligations.note: S.O. 1533(E) of 14 September 2006 remains the operative principal instrument. Appendix IV governs the hearing procedure.

obligations.requirement: Prior consent of at least 80% of affected families where land is acquired for a private company, and at least 70% where it is acquired for a public private partnership. The consent process runs alongside the Social Impact Assessment under section 4.
obligations.trigger: Government acquisition of land for a private company or a PPP. Does not apply to land bought through private negotiation.
obligations.note: Andhra Pradesh (Act 22 of 2018) and Maharashtra (Act 37 of 2018) each inserted a state section 10A removing this consent requirement for listed project categories. There is no section 10A in the central Act.

obligations.requirement: In a Scheduled Area, the prior consent of the Gram Sabha, Panchayat or Autonomous District Council must be obtained in ALL cases of land acquisition, including cases of urgency, before any notification issues under this or any other Act.
obligations.trigger: Any acquisition or alienation of land in a Fifth Schedule Scheduled Area.
obligations.note: This is consent, not consultation, and it is the strongest consent provision in the Indian land acquisition regime. Sections 41(1) and 41(2) additionally direct that acquisition in Scheduled Areas be avoided as far as possible and undertaken only as a demonstrable last resort.

obligations.requirement: A Social Impact Assessment must be prepared in consultation with the concerned Panchayat, Municipality or Municipal Corporation, with representation for the Gram Sabha, and appraised by an independent multi-disciplinary expert group.
obligations.trigger: Government acquisition of land under the Act.

obligations.requirement: Eleven elements of rehabilitation and resettlement entitlement for every affected family, over and above compensation: housing; land for land, with Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe families entitled to land equivalent to that acquired or 2.5 acres, whichever is lower; a choice of employment, a one-time payment, or an indexed annuity; a subsistence grant, with an additional sum for SC/ST families displaced from Scheduled Areas; transport, cattle-shed, artisan and resettlement allowances; and fishing rights in reservoirs.
obligations.trigger: Families displaced or affected within the meaning of section 3(c), where the land is acquired under the Act; acquired under an enactment in its Fourth Schedule (the Coal Bearing Areas, National Highways and Railways Acts among them), to which section 105(3) extends these terms; or purchased privately above the limit a State prescribes under section 2(3). Land already held, or bought below that limit, does not engage it.

obligations.requirement: The Gram Sabha or Panchayat at the appropriate level shall be CONSULTED before land is acquired in a Scheduled Area for a development project, and before affected persons are resettled or rehabilitated.
obligations.trigger: Land acquisition or resettlement in a Fifth Schedule Scheduled Area.
obligations.note: Consultation, not consent. The word 'consent' does not appear in PESA. PESA binds state legislatures rather than proponents directly, so its project-level effect runs through the State Panchayati Raj Act and State PESA Rules. Nine of the ten PESA states have notified Rules; Odisha has not.

obligations.requirement: The recommendation of the Gram Sabha or Panchayat is mandatory before the grant of a prospecting licence or mining lease for MINOR minerals in a Scheduled Area, and before any concession for exploiting minor minerals by auction.
obligations.trigger: Mining of MINOR minerals in a Fifth Schedule Scheduled Area. Major minerals - coal, iron ore, bauxite, limestone - are not covered by these clauses.
obligations.note: What is mandatory is obtaining the recommendation, not complying with it. The Act does not provide that an adverse recommendation defeats the grant.

obligations.requirement: Community Forest Resource rights - to protect, regenerate, conserve or manage customary common forest land - vest in the Gram Sabha and must be recognised before that land is treated as unencumbered.
obligations.trigger: Any project on or affecting forest land where forest rights have been claimed or are capable of being claimed.

obligations.requirement: Free informed consent of the Gram Sabhas concerned, obtained in writing, to any proposed resettlement and to the resettlement package. One of six cumulative conditions that must ALL be satisfied.
obligations.trigger: Resettlement of forest rights holders from a critical wildlife habitat in a National Park or Sanctuary, to create an inviolate area for wildlife conservation. This is NOT a general consent requirement for every forest diversion.

obligations.requirement: The Gram Sabha is the authority that initiates the process of determining the nature and extent of forest rights.

obligations.instrument: MoEF&CC circular under the Forest (Conservation) Act 1980
obligations.requirement: For proposals to divert forest land, evidence that the forest rights settlement process under the Forest Rights Act is complete, and the written consent of the Gram Sabhas concerned.
obligations.trigger: Diversion of forest land under the Forest (Conservation) Act 1980.
obligations.note: This is an ADMINISTRATIVE circular, a different source of obligation from the Act itself. Its current force is affected by the Van (Sanrakshan Evam Samvardhan) Adhiniyam 2023 and the 2023 Rules made under it, and by Ashok Kumar Sharma v. Union of India in the Supreme Court. Treat the position as contested and verify before relying on it.

obligations.requirement: Free, Prior and Informed Consent of affected Indigenous Peoples, not merely consultation, in defined circumstances: impacts on lands and natural resources subject to traditional ownership or customary use (paras 13-14); relocation from such lands (para 15); significant impacts on critical cultural heritage (para 16); and commercial use of cultural heritage or traditional knowledge (para 17).
obligations.trigger: A project affecting Indigenous Peoples, where the client is financed by IFC or by a lender applying the Performance Standards. PS7 paragraph 4 lists 'scheduled tribes' among the terms that may identify Indigenous Peoples.
obligations.note: The 2012 edition remains in force; a joint IFC/MIGA update launched in April 2025 has not been adopted. Two framings of the FPIC circumstances circulate: PS7 groups paragraphs 16-17 under one heading, giving THREE, while IFC's own Guidance Note 7 at GN27 enumerates FOUR. Both trace to paragraphs 13-17. Guidance Note 5 is the key point for India: applicability turns on the four characteristics in paragraph 5, and domestic legal recognition is expressly NOT a determining factor - so a group may engage PS7 whether or not Indian law calls it anything in particular.

obligations.instrument: IFC Performance Standard 5 (Land Acquisition and Involuntary Resettlement), 2012
obligations.requirement: Compensation at full replacement cost, with possession taken only after compensation is made available. A Resettlement Action Plan is required for physical displacement REGARDLESS OF THE NUMBER OF PEOPLE AFFECTED; a Livelihood Restoration Plan is required for economic displacement alone.
obligations.trigger: Physical or economic displacement where affected people do not have the right to refuse - including negotiated settlements reached in the shadow of expropriation. Genuinely voluntary market transactions are outside PS5.
obligations.note: Paragraph 17 recognises three categories of displaced person, including those with no recognisable legal right or claim. That reaches people Indian land acquisition law does not compensate, notably agricultural labourers who hold no land right.

obligations.provision: Principle 3, Principle 5, and the Scope section
obligations.requirement: For a project in a Non-Designated Country, compliance with the IFC Performance Standards in full, not merely with host country law. Principle 5 requires effective, culturally appropriate stakeholder engagement, Informed Consultation and Participation where impacts may be significant, and FPIC in the PS7 paragraph 13-17 circumstances - with a qualified independent consultant evaluating the process.
obligations.trigger: Project finance from US$10 million total capital cost, or project-related corporate loans where the aggregate loan and the individual lender's commitment are each at least US$50 million with a tenor of two years or more, provided a signatory institution is in the syndicate.
obligations.note: India is neither an OECD member nor on the World Bank high-income list, so it is a Non-Designated Country and the IFC Performance Standards apply in full rather than host-country law alone. DECISIVE FOR APPLICABILITY: of the 126 current signatories there is NO Indian institution. IDFC FIRST Bank was the only Indian signatory ever, from 2013 until it de-listed voluntarily in 2023. The Equator Principles therefore reach an Indian project only through a foreign lender. Note also that 'SBI Shinsei Bank' on the signatory list is Japanese and is not State Bank of India.

obligations.requirement: Recognition of the right of ownership, collective or individual, over the lands which tribal populations traditionally occupy, and a bar on removing them from those lands without their free consent save in accordance with national laws and regulations for reasons of national security or economic development, with lands of at least equal quality or full compensation provided.
obligations.trigger: Ratified by India and in force, so it binds the State in international law. It creates no directly enforceable project-level duty on a proponent, but it informs how the domestic regime is read.
obligations.note: INDIA HAS NOT RATIFIED ILO CONVENTION 169, the 1989 Indigenous and Tribal Peoples Convention that revised C107 and introduced the consultation and consent standards most often cited in this field. Verified directly against the ILO NORMLEX ratification table for India on 2026-08-22: C107 appears, ratified 29 September 1958 and in force; C169 does not appear at all. This is frequently reported wrongly. C107 was closed to further ratification once C169 entered force, so India remains bound by the older instrument, whose integrationist premise C169 was written to replace.

Until each Order has been read and its districts, blocks and villages transcribed, this instrument reports Scheduled Area status as not determined rather than inferring it.
